text:
Vegas won this one, but it was never close in the way that matters. The Golden Knights piled up 4.49 expected goals to Vancouver's 1.51 and took 60 shot attempts to 36, which works out to a team that wins about 91 percent of the time if you replay every shot. The Canucks were the 9 percent. They got there by scoring on a 5 percent chance, and still lost.

That chance was Jonathan Lekkerimäki's snap shot at 17:54 of the second, which tied it 2-2 and was the least likely goal of the night. Marc Gatcomb answered 34 seconds later at 18:28 on a 31 percent look, assisted by Braeden Bowman and Nic Dowd, and that was the winner. Before that, Paul Cotter had put Vancouver ahead on a power-play tip-in at 18:52 of the first (11 percent), Mitch Marner tied it at 9:01 of the second, and Victor Olofsson gave Vegas the lead on a power-play snap at 14:30 (32 percent).

The second period was where the gap showed. Vegas generated 2.14 expected goals to Vancouver's 0.54 and still needed a goal in the final two minutes to restore the lead. Olofsson was a driver, shooting four times and finishing with 2.28 expected goals for while his line was on the ice, against only 0.18 against. Kevin Lankinen faced 28 shots and stopped about 1.5 more than expected, which kept it a one-goal game. Adin Hill stopped 18 of 20 and allowed slightly more than the 1.51 he was expected to give up. Vancouver's 20 blocked shots and Lankinen's work held the score down, but the chances were mostly Vegas's.
